_comment: One list of identifier cases with one expected verdict each, read by all
three layers that enforce the scope-identifier grammar: Python's re (via
rights.py's IDENTIFIER_PATTERN), the JSON Schema at
core/equipment_identity/p0/rights_decision.schema.json (validated with the
jsonschema package, which compiles `pattern` with Python's own re), and
the Zod mirror in functions-equipment-identity/src/p1/contracts.ts (which
uses JavaScript's RegExp).
Each suite checks its own engine against THESE verdicts rather than
against another engine, so a divergence fails in whichever layer drifted
and names itself. Comparing the pattern strings would prove nothing: the
four cases marked cross-runtime below are exactly the inputs on which two
engines given byte-identical patterns return different answers.
cross-runtime, measured rather than assumed:
U+0085  Python's \S rejects it, JavaScript's accepts it
U+FEFF  Python's \S accepts it, JavaScript's rejects it
U+00A0  a non-ASCII space, whitespace to both but not in our alphabet
abc\n   Python's $ matches before a trailing newline, JavaScript's
does not -- which is why the grammar ends with (?![\s\S])
Escapes are written as \uXXXX rather than as literal characters so this
file survives an encoding round-trip on any platform.
snapshot_path_* and sha256_* were added after a review found that the
identifier grammar had been made portable while the two new evidence
fields had not: Python rejected a whitespace-only path that the JSON
Schema and Zod accepted, and all three still spelled the sha256 rule
with a $, which Python matches before a trailing newline. Parity that
covers only one field is not parity.
